The platform says the new AI training policy is aimed solely at improving storefronts and tools, but not everyone is buying it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Update: Etsy told the New York Times on Friday that it intends to revise the policy.

Online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from users over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models. In response, numerous vendors have closed their online shops, and are encouraging others to do the same. Etsy, however, says the new policy isn't meant to "replace your creativity," but simply to improve storefront operations.

The offending bit is found in part 5, section C of Etsy's terms of use, effective as of December 16:

That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew, it led to significant pushback from some Etsy users, including numerous store closures.

You might have heard of Etsy's new terms and artists fleeing the platform. We're out, too.

A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration)

In the wake of that reaction, Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman posted a separate update saying it's not really like that at all, and that "we do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity."

"When we describe how we may use your content, we're enabling actions like translating your listing descriptions so buyers around the world can discover your items, or featuring your listing photos in Etsy marketing campaigns to showcase your creative work," Ossman wrote. "We also use your content to develop tools that make running your shop easier, like listing optimization tools or stats summaries that help you better understand your shop's performance. As always, your needs and feedback help guide how we build and improve these tools."

As for providing third-party access to that content, Ossman said that too is for "services and tools that can help you run your business," and promised that "when we partner with third parties, we do so thoughtfully to help protect your content and data."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

That hasn't satisfied everyone. Ossman's commitment doesn't exist within the actual terms of service, which as seen above states only that Etsy and partners can "use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies." Ossman also noted in his update that the terms "prohibit scraping Etsy or unauthorized use of content from Etsy to train AI models," but that (as far as I can tell) applies to Etsy users and unauthorized third-parties, not Etsy itself or those it licenses.

That's not to suggest that Etsy is being underhanded, merely that the binding legal language is imprecise. Others also complain that AI training should be opt-in rather than on by default—and worse, there's apparently no opt-out option available at all, so users who are opposed to having their work used for AI training for any reason are out of luck.

Ironically, the blowup over Etsy's embrace of AI training comes just weeks after it earned plaudits for banning AI-generated recipes and patterns, a move Ossman said was necessary to establish "trust" in the platform: "Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it."

However this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.

I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the new AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.

For the last decade, Ben and Erin Napier have been renovating homes in the small Southern town of Laurel, Mississippi, on HGTV’s wildly popular show Home Town. The series’ 10th season premiered in January on the 2026 TV schedule, and fans, including me, have been itching for any sort of update on the famous reality couple. In particular, I’ve been waiting for an update on Season 11, and Erin finally spoke out.

Season 10 wrapped up in March, and Erin revealed in August that filming had just started back up on the new episodes. While there isn’t any information on when to expect Home Town''s exact return, there is one big piece of news that will surely make people happy: Erin took to her social channels earlier this week to share the episodes are just about done, and she even posted photos from the wrap party:

A post shared by Erin Napier (@erinapier)

Considering it’s been a trying year for the Napiers, it’s great to see them finally able to celebrate something. Last December, the hotel they were renovating for their series, Home Town: Inn This Together, caught on fire, close to Erin’s 40th birthday.

Fans were able to see the hard work the couple and their team have put into the hotel for the spinoff, which ended with the hotel fire (streaming now with an HBO Max subscription), but I love that they can look forward to the future of Home Town, which is certainly not slowing down any time soon thanks to the Napiers and their incredible team:

Season 10 will be all buttoned up in a couple of weeks but last night we celebrated. You all must know that there’s no way one person can manage the design processes of 9 houses at the same time, and so I get to lean on this incredible team. Together we make a plan then everyone goes on whatever journey the house gives them, shopping and making every design choice with me. They are the many eyes and hands and feet that get to these houses across the finish line and I get to be an editor in chief of sorts, and it feels like magic every time.

Welp, I didn't see this confusion coming. I’m excited to see what kind of houses the Napiers are renovating in the new season, which is billed as Season 10, but is actually Season 11. The Season 10 finale aired in March, so these new batch of episodes, coming sometime in 2027, will certainly be Season 11.

It's a little confusing, and the Home Town stars know it. Erin clarified why she referred to the new episodes as Season 10, rather than Season 11, when asked by a fan, and her response makes a lot of sense:

So, because of a programming discrepancy like 4 years ago, the numbers are off! y'all will know Season 10 as Season 11.

It’s definitely confusing, but I'm glad it was addressed. There are plenty of shows whose production numbers don’t line up with episode numbers, for whatever reason. For instance, a big Jeopardy! inconsistency Ken Jennings revealed last year was that the production numbers currently being used don’t equal the total number of episodes produced, all because of mistakes from decades ago.

Regardless, I’m relieved to know production is just about wrapped, meaning we’ll be getting the Napiers back on our TVs soon. It's also worth noting, new seasons of Home Town typically premiere in December or January, and since the new season is still being worked on for the next couple of weeks, if the pattern sticks, we could be looking the same timeline for Season 10 (11). For now, the wait continues!

Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3797. Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - founded by ex-GTA veteran - has a mountain of debt, and the main plan for paying it back is litigation

"A coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary."

Beleaguered Mindseye developer Build a Rocket Boy - the company created by former Rockstar and Grand Theft Auto producer Leslie Benzies - apparently owes approximately £62 million in debt. And a huge chunk of that appears to be owed to Chinese gaming company NetEase (£36.5m), though more than £1m appears to be owed to Benzies himself.

This came to light in a proposal issued by Build a Rocket Boy's administrators this week (spotted by Resetera), which lists both the moneys owed (right down to a £20 charge to OpenAI) and details what went wrong, as well as what Build a Rocket Boy intends to do to recoup money to pay the debts back. And the company's "largest" potential asset, according to the administrators, is litigation.

"Prior to the Company's entry into Administration, the directors had been investigating circumstances surrounding the commercial performance of the video game, MindsEye, which was released in 2025 following significant development investment," the administration proposal read. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary.

"The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that any such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions."

This tallies with the narrative spun by co-company leader Mark Gerhard as the company waded into deep water. Gerhard blamed "organised espionage and corporate sabotage" for the studio's difficulties as multiple rounds of layoffs shredded Build a Rocket Boy. "People had their hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around the product," Gerhard said.

The situation he's referring to is likely the alleged smear campaign made against the game, which Gerhand reportedly claimed in an internal meeting this year was paid for by a "big American company" and then run by a UK company called Ritual Network, which apparently had influencers, journalists and staff at Build a Rocket Boy deliberately sabotage the game's release. That's according to an account of a videoed internal meeting reportedly seen by Insider Gaming earlier this year.

It had nothing to do with the dire state of Mindseye when it launched, then. Eurogamer awarded it one out of five stars, chastising its "ridiculous story, inconsistent writing, poorly designed mission scenarios, and utterly atrocious combat" in our Mindseye review.

Build a Rocket Boy was founded in 2016, and its first game, Everywhere - a sort of online gaming platform - was announced in 2022. It never materialised, but a part of that vision was carved out to become a standalone game experience of its own along the way, and that's how we got Mindseye - a take on a Grand Theft Auto formula. Whether or not the litigation is successful and can recoup any of Build a Rocket Boy's debts remains to be seen, but there's a financial mountain for the studio to climb if it hopes to operate again.

The GTA 6 Snap Tool is an essential item which lets you get into locked doors without setting off alarms

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6.

The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most important piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it.

The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City.

If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked.

The Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door.

It's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit.

#3795. Infinity Nikki fans threaten to boycott game after promotion by Elon Musk's mother, but there may be a genuine reason for her involvement

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, cozy, open-world dress-up game, is at the centre of controversy again, though this time not because fans disliked one of the game's updates. Instead, it's because of… Elon Musk's mother.

Some Infinity Nikki fans are planning to boycott the game following the release of the game's latest trailer, which is narrated by Maye Musk. The trailer is for a new update - dubbed Cicia - which adds the ability to drive futuristic hovering cars. The reveal comes days after a widely mocked demonstration of Musk's own Tesla "flying car", which doesn't actually fly.

While some fans are worried Tesla's cars may be coming to the game, many also simply don't want their game associated with Elon Musk and his family.

"If they promote Tesla or mention him in the game I'm 100 percent dropping it," wrote one Reddit user (via The Gamer). "Why would they involve that man in a girly fashion game, and if they wanted a car brand partnership why not a Chinese one??!? Infold is addicted to negative attention I swear."

"If Tesla is somehow involved in the design of the car (or worse, an in-game promotion), then I might have to let go," wrote another person in the same thread. "Please please please be wrong."

Though Maye Musk's involvement might seem random, there may be a good explanation for it. "Here's something that might surprise people who only know her as Elon's mother: Maye Musk is a celebrity in China in her own right," Reddit user BarbieSpeedRacer explained.

"She's a successful model, an author, and a recognisable advertising personality. Her memoir became popular with Chinese readers, and she's appeared in campaigns and promotional events for brands including OPPO, Fila, and JNBY."

Her image as "a woman in her seventies who continues to work as a fashion model" is one that resonates with the game's Chinese audience, apparently, especially "among women interested in fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content".

"A Chinese company makes an advertisement featuring a celebrity popular in China, and an international fandom interprets that decision almost exclusively through the lens of American domestic politics," the post added.

So far, calls for a boycott don't appear to have coalesced into a movement, at least judging by the game's subreddit. Even if Western players were to organise one, it's not likely to hurt Infinity Nikki much, as most of the game's revenue - estimated at more than 80 percent - comes from Chinese players.

In Eurogamer's Infinity Nikki review, Jessica Orr said it advances the genre of open-world gacha games and brings competition to rival developer miHoYo, writing: "The changes in length, combat and progression all feel utterly invigorating compared to other Genshin-likes, and it's why Infinity Nikki feels like it could (and should) be on the same trajectory to shake up the gacha scene just like Genshin Impact did in 2020."

Preorders of GTA 6 totalled approximately 32.5 million copies.

Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar says the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history."

By way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."

Strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously said that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics. It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a new record across all platforms."

Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day—surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end.

Given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit.

Here's how you can clone keys in GTA 6 and finally make some real money

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you're looking to upgrade the quality of the car you're driving around Leonida in, there's a good chance you're wondering how to clone keys in GTA 6. While you can steal basic vehicles right from the beginning of the game, either by smashing the window or using a slim jim, keyless cars require specialist equipment before you're able to make off with the ride.

With that in mind, I'm going to explain how to get the GTA 6 Key Cloner and how you can use it to steal more expensive vehicles.

The GTA 6 Key Cloner isn't available until you progress into Chapter 3 of the GTA 6 Mission list. It's the 17th main story mission where you'll be asked to Steal the Zorrusso For Randy, a new vehicle fence who will pay top-dollar for luxury cars and will even ask you to collect rare vehicles on his behalf.

To do that, you'll need to be able to clone keys in GTA 6. Randy will install the Key Cloner application on your phone as part of this mission. It isn't possible to clone keys until you have reached this point.

With the Key Cloner application installed on your phone, you're now able to get inside nicer cars and drive them away. Use the WAiNK app on your phone by holding Up on the D-pad to identify whether a car requires a key cloner to get inside, and whether the vehicle has any security trackers.

So long as you have the Key Cloner, just walk up to the driver's side door and press Triangle/Y to begin cloning the key. You'll need to rotate the right-thumbstick until you find the sweet spot, which will be indicated by a lour whirring sound and rumble in your controller. You're now able to get inside without setting off the car alarm.

Just because you can get inside a keyless vehicle easily enough, it doesn't mean that there aren't consequences. This class of vehicle will typically have trackers installed, which can be identified by pressing up on the D-pad once you're behind the wheel (look underneath the vehicle name).

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Standard Trackers are easy enough to deal with, so long as you don't attract the attention of the police. It's worth noting that you are restricted from making modifications to cars with standard trackers, at least until you drive them to Randy's garage and register it as a personal vehicle in GTA 6.

Advanced Trackers are more of a problem. These will ping your exact location to cops as soon as you begin to drive too slowly. You also won't be able to fence (or own) this class of vehicle until you've progressed far enough through Randy's Wish List of stolen cars – Advanced Trackers are too hot to handle until then.

#3792. You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"

You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5, but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title.

You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a new manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting.

It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," says David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style."

That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply.

In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear.

GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here. If you want to, ahem, 'travel to New Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you.

It's an honor to be the answer to a question on Jeopardy!, and I'd assume it's an even higher honor to be the answer for Final Jeopardy! So, with that in mind, it's always fun to see how people react to being the subject of a question featured on the show. Case in point: Ice-T had a very funny take when he found out that someone didn't know he was the answer to Final Jeopardy!.

Final Jeopardy! can literally make or break someone’s future on the long-running game show. The clues can range from history to literature to, yes, even pop culture. On the episode from the 2026 TV schedule that aired on October 28, Ice-T was the answer for the final round. Two people got it right, but one person was wrong. Ice-T addressed the moment while appearing on the Today Show and revealed just what he thinks of the whole ordeal:

I’m in a lot of crossword puzzles, because Ice-T, I-C-E-T, is a weird spelled thing. But Jeopardy, I’ve been in Jeopardy before, but Final Jeopardy. …. [They asked] who put out an album, Home Invasion, and also is the longest-running character in television. And the guy said Tim Allen. I think he was thinking about Home Improvement, right? But the two women got it right, and I only care about the women [laughs]. So, you know, he lost, and they won. But that’s how it goes. But Final Jeopardy!’s a big deal.

Of course, being a clue on Jeopardy! is a big deal, even if it does sting when someone does not know the answer. And as Ice-T pointed out, he’s been in plenty of clues over the years. That being said, it’s a lot different when you’re in Final Jeopardy!

Overall, I love that Ice-T wasn’t too hurt over being mistaken for Tim Allen, and instead focused on the fact that the two women got it right, which is all he cares about. I'm also very entertained by the image of Tim Allen trying to rap.

Anyway, the clue was for the category “Current TV Streaks,” and it just shows that even if a clue seems easy, it may not be for a lot of people. For host Ken Jennings, there was one category that made him nervous when he was competing, and it was surprisingly hockey. While he wound up being one of the biggest Jeopardy! winners of all time and no one has yet to beat his 74-game streak, it sounds like that still haunts him. So, everyone has their blind spots.

Meanwhile, that Final Jeopardy! clue made me realize something truly insane. Despite the fact that Law & Order: SVU is in its 28th season, it’s wild to me that Ice-T has been playing Odafin “Fin” Tutuola for almost three decades. He’s been on the NBC drama since the second season and is one of the longest-running actors in the Law & Order franchise. Luckily, he doesn’t have any plans to leave any time soon. While he has been worried that he’d be written out as the show has had to make room for Kellie Giddish, that has not been the case.

Hopefully, the next time Ice-T is an answer for Final Jeopardy! everyone gets it right. However, even if it’s just the women, I’m sure he will be just fine. In the meantime, fans can catch him on Law & Order: SVU on Thursday, December 3, at 9 p.m. ET on NBC, streaming the next day with a Peacock subscription.

#3790. Just how detailed is the audio in GTA 6? Well, even convenience store refrigerators "all have their own unique sounds", says Rockstar dev

If you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is currently fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped, one thing quickly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into.

It's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain. It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time". But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound.

"Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment."

This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor.

He goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor.

GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

It's easier to make successful games when you hold onto the people who know how.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

From Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees said that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the company enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on unionization.

Sick of Jason and Lucia getting covered in pink dye every time they touch a Marked Bill? Then you need the GTA 6 Dye-Pack Jammer

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Have you tried robbing a bank or loan store in Vice City, and made off with a duffel bag of marked bills, only to find that Jason and Lucia get covered in pink paint once they've made a successful getaway? If you're sick of this happening to you, then you need to get yourself a Dye-Pack Jammer in GTA 6.

This essential piece of equipment is used to disable the signal transmitted by dye-packs, which are attached to all marked bills from high-end robbery locations across Leonida. You'll know if you're at risk of getting marked – making yourself exceedingly obvious to patrolling cops, at least until you can change your appearance – because you'll hear a sharp beeping noise just before the explosion. It's classic GTA 6.

You will unlock the GTA 6 Dye-Pack Jammer as part of the main story progression. You'll need to complete Credit Check, which is Chapter 3's 16th mission in GTA 6. You'll collect the equipment from a character named Karim, and it is not missable. This is the only way you can unlock the Dye-Pack Jammer in GTA 6.

Once you've unlocked the Dye-Pack Jammer in the Credit Check mission, you'll now be able to steal Marked Bills from Banks and Payday Loan locations. While it's possible to acquire Marked Bills before this, none of the GTA 6 fence locations will accept them and they will more often than not result in you getting pink dye all over your clothes.

Once you have the Dye-Pack Jammer, you're free to rob who and what you like. And you never need to fear the risk of getting covered in dye ever again. So it's well worth progressing early into Chapter 3 to get this item as soon as you're able to.

The love, joy and merriment of the holiday season are always infectious in theme parks. As part of Universal Epic Universe’s holiday celebration expansion for 2026, the decorations have been scaled up (sorry, I had to work a dragon reference in there) in How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk for Snoggletog, and guests are all the better for it.

I got to experience the newborn theme park’s first holiday season in 2025, which was festive but also promised so much future possibility. Seeing what Universal was able to pull together just six months into the opening of their newest theme park just made me want more of everything. At that time, Snoggletog was relegated to a banner hung in the Isle of Berk gift shop that you could miss and never know it was there if you didn’t wander inside. So, I was particularly excited to learn that this year, the annual holiday inspired by modern Christmas traditions would be expanded throughout the land.

For those not in the know, Snoggletog is the winter holiday celebrated by the Viking community on the fictional Isle of Berk in the How to Train Your Dragon franchise. It features feasts and festivities fit for dragons and even includes the seasonal Harvest Mac & Cheese Cone at Hooligan’s Grog & Gruel. And there’s now a row of trees, just inside the entrance, decorated with what looks to be homemade ornaments that are a fun detail to check out during the day and beautiful to look at once they’re lit up at night.

Epic Universe is already a big award winner and popular destination with a ton of great attractions. I appreciate that they’re not wasting any time by expanding their offerings, too, even with something that seems as small as holiday decorations. (Not to mention there’s that construction on an Epic Universe expansion for an indoor coaster.)

While my own gothic heart remains in Darkmoor, through the Dark Universe portal, Isle of Berk feels like the most expansive and detailed area of Epic Universe, so it’s especially nice to see this holiday celebration get the extra attention it deserves. It’s true, Toothless has yet to don a Santa hat, but you never know what could be added next year and into the future.

You can check out a video overview of Snoggletog during the daytime via Orlando Informer below:

A post shared by Orlando Informer (@orlandoinformer)

I have to say, the thing that most caught my eye was the wreath full of apples. It’s the perfect decor idea that not only looks beautifully festive but would also just be delicious. I also love that you can find a tree made of wood inside Hiccup’s Workshop that you could probably easily replicate if you’re crafty, or you can just pick up themed ornaments for your own home holiday tree.

If you’re going to be in Orlando in the near future, you can experience Snoggletog at Epic Universe and then head over to the Universal Orlando Resort, where you can have a very merry Grinchmas while also rounding out your theme park trip with what is the best theme park holiday parade through January 3, 2027.

#3784. GTA 6 breaks the all-time livestream viewer record hours before it's available to play for most of the world

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

According to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in New Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 launches officially in more regions of the world.

If you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

This doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

It's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

There's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

While you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

#3782. 10 Shows Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

What started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Plan on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole new persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

This is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Blending the Big Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

The tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

#3781. GTA 6 is so big, it managed to break Reddit - and it isn't even actually out yet

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't even out yet, and it's already causing some technical issues over at the game's official Reddit page.

In a post verified by r/GTA6 moderators and pinned to the page, user and moderator PapaXah wrote "GTA 6 broke Reddit", and explained that "many things" were currently busted at the time of the post. Looking through Reddit, many flairs (little labels attached to posts) aren't loading properly and appear as a string of code rather than proper images. PapaXah also replied to one user suggesting they make real flairs based on these busted flairs, writing: "Reddit's so broken I couldn't even do it. We actually have a bunch of new flairs that I can't even upload."

Another moderator, TekS, also acknowledged that some user's posts may not be viewable as a result of ongoing strain on Reddit during GTA 6's release. They commented: "If you can't post/comment or see your user flair, well, know that it's perfectly normal."

Ahead of the game's full launch across the world, the Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken viewership records across streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Interesting details about the game are also trickling out, including the fact that different refrigerators have their own unique sounds. Video games, ladies and gentlemen.

With Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

If you want to get into yellow containers in GTA 6 to find secret vehicle stashes and weapons caches, you'll need the Cut-Off Tool first

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Have you noticed that there's these yellow cargo containers all over Leonida? Did you know that you can actually get inside of them to get rare weapons, explosives, vehicles, and so much more! It's yet another one of those hidden aspects of GTA 6 that you can't help but go out of your way to find more of, once you know to start looking.

If you want to break into yellow Scoop containers in GTA 6, you're going to need to get a vital piece of equipment first: the Cut-Off Tool. Below I'm going to walk you through how to unlock the GTA 6 Cut-Off Tool and explain how it can be used to break into those Scoop containers.

The Cut-Off Tool is one of the main pieces of GTA 6 equipment that you'll unlock as you play through the story. While you'll likely come across those yellow Scoop containers in your travels, you won't be able to open any of them until you've played a key GTA 6 mission in Chapter 3. Meet the Heders is the third mission of that chapter, and it'll send you down to a dockyard. Once you're these, you'll automatically be assigned the equipment and can use it freely outside of the mission.

You need to locate yellow Scoop shipping containers. These can be in the most unlikely of places – on random beaches, next to gang hideouts, in random parking lots – all across Leonida. Once you've located one, walk up to its front doors and press Triangle/Y. This will prompt Jason or Lucia to equip the Cut-Off Tool. You'll need to squeeze R2/RT and keep the power within the pink segment of the semi-circle for a short while until you cut through the lock. Once you do, the doors will swing open and you're welcome to whatever you find inside.

#3779. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

One of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

Compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

The iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

For years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

Screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

If you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you plan to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more important to get a high-quality one.

If you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also important to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

The hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

One of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

The outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

However, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

#3778. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar staff appear in GTA 6 game credits, though some aren't listed as "former employees", curiously

UPDATE: The final few names have been confirmed.

UPDATE 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6. We were able to confirm the final few names' existence there after Rockstar posted the full credits online - in searchable form. Before this, the process of cross-checking was intensely laborious: it required watching a scrolling list of names for an hour-and-a-half to see if they appeared.

Also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know. These names appear listed under the departments the people worked for, as if they still worked at Rockstar. Why this is, we don't know - perhaps it's something to do with being involved in the employment tribunal or not. We're asking Rockstar for clarification.

ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is currently facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the company making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

But perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union."

Universal Epic Universe is currently celebrating its second holiday season with more holiday decorations than last year and a new Dark Universe ride currently under construction. There’s even more gifts from the theme park during this time of merriment! It’s just been announced that for the first time ever Epic is going to be added into the Annual Pass mix. The news led to a mix of huge excitement and tons of questions.

In a Universal Parks announcement, the Orlando resort shared that annual passes featuring Universal Epic Universe access are coming in early December. Guests with current annual passes will be able to upgrade their current passes, and those looking to purchase one can do so at this time. Unlike the other parks, there will be a reservation system in place with the earliest date to go with a pass being January 4, 2027. Check out some of the spirited reactions from Twitter:

Ever since Epic Universe opened its gates in May of last year, it has quickly become a favorite park with tons of great rides to check out. For those who want to return there again and again (and perhaps make time to notice the park’s fun easter eggs) an annual pass is always a great value. Fans are rightfully hyped.

Whenever there’s a big change at one of Universal Orlando’s parks, inquiries typically follow, and there’s a lot popping up amidst the announcement. Here’s a few big ones:

Universal was all over the comment section trying to answer some of these questions. Most of them seem to point to there being another wave of details on the way, but for now Universal Orlando’s Annual Pass website has been refreshed with current steps to take if you'd like to upgrade.

Universal Orlando Resort will still offer four different types of pass tiers, but the announcement includes a complete re-branding of the system. Those who hold these memberships will be called “Pass Members” rather than “Passholders” and the type names will go from being called Seasonal, Power, Preferred and Premier to Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum. They’re also going completely digital with all physical passes being phased out over time.

In regards to the Epic Universe upgrade, current Passholders will be given a timeframe for when they can upgrade their passes, and current holders will be able to switch before anyone else. Those who are in their renewal period will also have the option to “pay a price difference of $125 to $410 to renew into a Pass with Universal Epic Universe access, depending on Pass type.” Annual passes currently cost between $475 and $1015, based on that price difference info; the price range might have changed to between $600 to $1425, but all the details are not yet clear to anyone quite yet.

Universal is already teasing more information on the way “soon." Either way, it’s quite exciting that those interested will soon get to enjoy Epic Universe over and over.

#3776. PSA: Some GTA 6 Ultimate Edition content is only available for the first chapter, and you'll have to put in hard graft to unlock more

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:

Rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take."

It's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

Looks like Lawrence Sullivan settled his differences with Rockstar.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot.

Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar "we gotta talk" and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action. Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: "Let me voice the character, give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man."

It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6.

"I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!"

"Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!"

A post shared by Florida joker 🃏 (@floridaajoker)

I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely.

Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending.

#3774. Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar says

Don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other big productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

"While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, said in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity."

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

The slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again."

If you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to New Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.
