Learning how to buy, manage, and equip a mask in GTA 6 is vital for losing some of your Appearance Heat

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you want to be a better criminal in Leonida, you're going to need to learn how to get a mask in GTA 6. Despite Rockstar making appearance a key factor in the new Wanted system, the game isn't super clear on the steps you can take to hide your identity – particularly as you're progressing through Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 missions list. Thankfully, I'm here to help you understand how to get neckwear in GTA 6, how to equip masks, and how to change them for new ones.

You can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores. Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento sells them (look at the central stand with the alligator head atop of it) from the beginning of the game, but you can head to any Ammu-Nation retailer to find more. Open up the GTA 6 Index, head into the weapons tab, and you'll be able to find all the relevant shops on your map. When you begin exploring Vice City and Vice Beach, you'll also find thrift stores that sell novelty masks, and high-end retailers which sell very fancy (and expensive) coverings that can be worn as well.

To wear a mask in GTA 6, you need to make sure that it's with you. You can add neckwear items to your loadout by visiting the wardrobe in your residences. Scroll to the accessories tab and that's where you'll find the Masks option, which separates them by brand. If you want options while you're on the road, you can also store some in the trunk of your personal vehicle in GTA 6 by highlighting it and pressing Square/X.

With a mask in your loadout, wearing it is as simple as holding L1/LB to open your loadout. Press R1/RB to scroll to the items menu, and then select Mask from the neckwear slot located at twelve-o'clock in the wheel. Press A to put it on, press A to remove it. Easy enough, and vital if you want to lose some of your Appearance Heat after robbing a store with CCTV equipment.

While hovering over the neckwear slot of your loadout, you can also press up and down to change the wear style of your mask in GTA 6. The first will see the mask conceal your face, which will draw panicked reactions from shop clerks, while the second will let you fashion the mask more appropriately.

"...literally allergic to anything like that. "

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We know Robert Pattinson is on Christopher Nolan’s “nice list” considering he’s cast the actor in two of his movies. (Did you know Pattinson even helped inspire Nolan to make Oppenheimer?) While the pair seem to have a great filmmaking partnership going, there was one time on the set of The Odyssey where Nolan totally rejected one choice Pattinson was hoping for on the spot.

Pattinson, of course, plays the very deplorable Antinous in The Odyssey. Before cameras started rolling, the actor reached out to the hair department to request a long wig for the part. As the movie’s hair department head Gloria Casny told it, when he called she just happened to be standing right next to Nolan. In her words:

I didn't even know how he got my number… The answer was no.

That’s right. No conversation or negotiations, just “no”. Casny told the story during a news conference for The Odyssey in promotion of it becoming one of the latest 2026 movies that’s available to watch at home. The story led Matt Damon, who was the event’s moderator, to make this comment:

It's funny because he knows Chris and he’s worked with Chris… Chris is literally allergic to anything like that.

I can definitely see Pattinson’s vision for Antinous, but apparently one of Nolan’s rules is he doesn’t like to have actors wear any wigs or fake facial hair. Makes sense for the filmmaker who famously tries to do as much of his movies practically as possible.

There’s been a few other stories around Nolan and Pattinson that have also come out before. For example, he’s reportedly the only cast member who asked to read the script. Also, Mia Goth told a story about how one time on set Pattinson approached Nolan with a question while they were filming and Nolan simply responded with “That’s your department, mate”. Nolan has a different way of working than most, but that’s got to be one reason he’s considered one of our best living filmmakers.

Pattinson wasn’t the only actor on the set of The Odyssey that made a request to the hair department. As Matt Damon told USA Today during the same event, he had actually asked Nolan if he could have a fake beard to play Odysseus. Can you guess Nolan’s answer? Per Damon’s words:

He just looked at me like, 'No.’ He’s like, ‘Just grow your beard.’ He likes everything real. To be fair, given the amount of time spent in the ocean and water alone, the hand-laid beard would never have worked. Where you’re just out in the elements all the time, it just wouldn’t have made sense.

Same reaction! How funny. Damon really did grow a magnificent beard though, so it all worked out. And, honestly Pattinson’s forward-swept bangs fit perfectly, too. You can appreciate the lack of wigs on The Odyssey by purchasing it for home viewing now.

#3771. GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

We'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

GTA 6's map is so big it's going to take months for people to comb through it and find everything. Rockstar has already posted the full map of Leonida online, but it doesn't answer one simple question that I know we've all been wondering: How long would it take to fly across this entire thing in a plane?

The answer is a lot less time than it would take to go by car, but still long enough to give you an idea of the sheer scale we're working with here. Using the closest plane to Jason's house, my trip across Leonida took around 4 minutes and 18 seconds, which is a little under an hour of in-game time. You can watch the entire flight from start to finish below.

Keep in mind that the Mammoth Dodo seaplane that carried me from the southern tip of the archipelago to the northern tip of the map is just one type of plane in GTA 6. I would bet there are faster options if you really want to zoom.

Even though I'm still very early in the GTA 6's story, I didn't have to go too far out of my way to test this. Jason's house is conveniently located pretty close to a spot with perfectly unattended planes to borrow. The Sunbelt Highway that runs south of it will lead you right to the earliest planes and helicopters you can find. Just don't fly over the nearby military base (trust me, it's bad news) and you'll be fine.

Rockstar compared GTA 6's map to its previous games, describing it as about the size of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined. Despite knowing this beforehand, I was still shocked to see how the map kept going when I first opened it up. Four minutes might not sound like a lot, but the enormity of it all sinks in as you glide above densely populated cities and neighborhoods that could be the setting of their own standalone videogames.

My experiment has left the fog of war on my map split into two halves. My flight path carved a line of partially revealed locations straight through it. I don't expect to clear the rest out for dozens of hours, but now I'm tempted to find out how long of a roadtrip it would be to do the same journey by car.

#3769. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!)

While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

“Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

A more modern issue with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

The term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Quickly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

If all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

It’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe big retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a big box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a new TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—big-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out quickly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

#3768. Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another company's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a company mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its plan with each new GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

Shaking Mattia's hand seems like quite an important moment in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The chance to shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6 comes up right at the start of the mission Day Release, seemingly like a key decision that might affect the tone of the rest of the mission and future job prospects. Multiple GamesRadar+ writers have gone through both options, and it's a lot less important of a decision in GTA 6 than you think, so here's what we know about the significance of shaking Mattia's hand.

Be aware of some very mild spoilers for later missions in Chapter 1 below.

Shaking Mattia's hand in GTA 6 makes no difference to any events in the Day Release mission. If you shake his hand, you shake his hand, and if you don't, you don't. Mattia doesn't even acknowledge that you left him hanging.

Later in the mission, Mattia offers Jason and Lucia some drugs in a nightclub and, again, accepting or refusing has no clear repercussions. Comparing videos of the choices side-by-side, there were no obvious differences between either outcome as the same thing happens regardless - Mattia either takes the drugs back or hands them over, stands up and leaves, then Jason and Lucia take to the dancefloor. The rest of the mission then plays out as normal.

As far as I can tell, turning Mattia down in either of these situations in Day Release has no long-term impact either as the "job" that he mentions at the end of the mission is critical to the story and can't be avoided. Just make sure you've done everything before the GTA 6 Tourist Trap mission as it's an important one – and if you get stuck, my GTA 6 Tourist Trap walkthrough can help.

We've also got loads of other GTA 6 guides for you to read if you're ever stuck.

#3766. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Warning! The following contains spoilers from the Survivor episode "Wilder Than A Cat In A Bathtub." Stream the episode with a Paramount+ subscription, and read at your own risk!

Survivor's coin flip remains a controversial addition to the game, as fans debate the pros and cons of what it brings to the CBS series. I initially didn't have issues with what went down with Lewis Kelly in Season 51's flip, until I learned there was more than one flip involved.

Lewis spoke to Rob Has A Podcast about his exit and was asked if he'd pick water over fire if he flipped the coin again in a future season. The third juror revealed that he didn't have to think about the hypothetical, because he flipped the coin twice the night of his elimination. Hear the story below:

Well, here's the thing. I did actually do it once [before the one shown] and it didn't land in the circle, and I hear 'fire.' And maybe I should've changed it. I didn't think about it, so, it's tough.

Lewis had to flip the coin twice, and the first time it landed on fire! Unfortunately, because it didn't land primarily in the circle placed on the ground, it was negated and he had to flip it again. Lewis didn't say how he felt about that, but I can say that as a Survivor fan, I'm pissed.

Survivor 51's Kilby Lost All Of His Worldly Possessions After A Wild Storage Wars Scheme Went South

I went back and watched Survivor, and Jeff Probst said that the contestant who correctly called the coin flip won immunity, an idol, and the grand prize went up another million. The only rule was that it had to land on what he called. At no point was it said the coin had to land on the mat, which wasn't even used for the shot of Lewis' coin flip.

Jeff's word is law on Survivor, and if he's allowed to push contestants to admit they like fire challenges on-camera, he should've honored the result of the initial coin flip. Obviously, they faked it for the camera that he took the flip a second time on camera. They should've stuck with his original flip result and just filmed until he recreated it in the way they wanted it shot.

To me, multiple flips for the coin feel sketchy. Sure, Lewis had a 50/50 shot both times, and one flip didn't impact the outcome of the other. At the same time, Lewis won the first flip and had it negated by something that wasn't part of the rules. Is it then fair that his odds of survival went back to 50% for a redo?

Now, there's also a third option here in which the mat and all of that was explained to Lewis ahead of the flip, and maybe that's why he wasn't as bent out of shape as I am. I'll also admit he was one of my favorites, so I'm also sad about seeing him head to the jury before this season wraps up on the 2026 TV schedule.

Survivor's Open Era continues to be full of surprises, which certainly keeps both the contestants and viewers on their toes. I think the biggest disappointment with this coin flip is that the payoff was pushed to next season. Right now, all we have to fester on is disappointment, and the fact that someone threw away their chance to stay in the game on a coin flip. We'll see what happens next Wednesday, and how Lewis' exit will impact the group dynamic.

The company says its new generative AI training agreement will only be used for good. Why would anyone believe that?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers.

This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business."

I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a company hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases.

The new agreement—which Etsy has told The New York Times it's planning to revise—says that Etsy and its third-party partners have the right to use uploaded content "to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe."

That reads to me like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. The tacked-on note about keeping users safe does nothing to limit what Etsy can do.

The artists who sell cool custom keycaps and other fun things on Etsy are already likely to struggle against knock-off sellers if they get popular enough. That came with the territory of online selling even before AI, but it is absurd to now insist that they willingly hand over all the things that make their stores unique—their art, their product descriptions—to systems capable of duplicating those things in hard-to-trace ways, with only a pinky swear to protect them.

We've all seen how the AI industry has tried to brush off the concerns of artists and others whose work it ingests. One company went so far as to create a chatbot bearing the name of a former PC Gamer editor without permission, pretending that this robo-editor could give writing advice like the real person. And that's without him even knowing they were doing it!

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Even if Etsy truly does have good intentions, expecting artists to give this the thumbs up is ridiculous. It is not their responsibility to improve the platform by letting it mimic their creative work. The revised terms should, at the very least, exclude every seller from AI training as the default setting.

#3763. It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

As pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the big release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is important. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either."

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe."

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

If you've been having a look around in the Progress section of the GTA 6 Index, you've most likely spotted the Equipment tab. There are 12 unique pieces of Equipment in GTA 6, all of it essential for finding new ways to explore the map and generally being a better criminal.

While all of the GTA 6 Equipment unlocks progressively throughout the main GTA 6 missions list, if you're feeling a little impatient I'm here to help you understand what's coming later down the line. I'm going to detail what each piece of equipment does in GTA 6, how it can be used, and where it can be unlocked.

The Binoculars in GTA 6 can be used to scope out enemy targets, mark enemies on the map, identify animals from afar, and even let you participate in a little bird watching (there are 60 of them in total across Leonida). The Binoculars can be equipped at all times from your loadout by holding L1/LB and selecting them from there.

The Flashlight in GTA 6 can be used to help bring a little light to dark buildings and the world itself at night. Admittedly, it's a little cumbersome, so consider going to an Ammu-Nation and fitting a torch to one of your weapons. If you don't want to go that route, then open your loadout with L1/LB, scrolls to where the binoculars are; use left and right on the D-pad on the equipment slot to select the flashlight.

Stash bags are essential in GTA 6, letting Jason and Lucia get out from banks and other robbery targets with more than $20,000 in Pocket Cash. Each character can hold up-to two duffel bags at any one time, and any narcotics, jewellery, or marked bills you pick up will automatically be thrown inside. Stash bags have different capacities, which are determined depending on the size of the building you're robbing.

As soon as you're able to free-roam the world in the Gear Up mission, you're free to purchase a pair of headphones. This is entirely optional, but buying headphones in GTA 6 will let you listen to music and podcasts outside of a vehicle. Purchase headphones and earbuds at any electronics store in the world for both Jason and Lucia – just beware: these can be knocked off your head and become lost.

Have you noticed any sealed wooden crates in your travels across Leonida? Well, more often than not they can actually be broken into – often containing ammunition, weapons, collectibles, and more. You'll get the Pry Bar added to your loadout during Chapter 3, where it will equip automatically as soon as Jason or Lucia approach an openable wooden box.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The Gear Up mission in Chapter 1 is your first opportunity to purchase a mask. These are used to help conceal Jason and Lucia's identities during robberies. While you will unlock a couple throughout the story, you can buy them early or accrue more of them in different styles. You can learn how to buy a mask here, which also has tips on how to equip and fashion them in different ways.

The Metal Detector is a piece of equipment that you'll need if you want to participate in a side-activity called Underwater Discoveries. Thankfully, this isn't something that you need to purchase. Instead, it'll become a part of your life after you begin doing work for Kenton as part of the main story, and can later be equipped from owned or borrowed boats before you head underwater.

The Slim Jim is a vital piece of equipment. Up until the Moses mission in Chapter 2, the only way you could steal a car was by smashing in its window – a noisy activity which draws attention. The vehicle fence will give you this item for free, allowing you to silently break into cars. It equips automatically whenever you approach a relevant car, and you can learn more about how to use a Slim Jim here.

The Snap Gun isn't available from the beginning of the game, but is well worth pushing into Chapter 3 for. During the Boobie's Time mission, you'll be introduced to a jewellery fence named Yasmani. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that you can help him with a few robberies. Once you've learned how to get the Snap Gun in GTA 6, you'll be able to open locked doors without setting off alarms.

Early on into Chapter 3, you'll have the option to go and meet Brian and Lori. You'll later find yourself down at the docklands, to break into yellow Scoop containers. From that point on, the equipment is yours to keep. You can learn more about how to use the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 here, and also find more information on what it can be used to break into later on.

You'll want to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 as fast as you can. This handy phone application is what you'll use to break into more modern vehicles, keyless cars that aren't going to be stolen through mere hotwiring alone. It takes a little while to reach the relevant mission in Chapter 3, but I would recommend you push through the story to get here if you want more to do in the world.

Have you tried robbing any Marked Bills without a Dye Pack Jammer? If yes, you've probably had to go home to change your clothes and have a shower to get the pink dye off. The Dye Pack Jammer automatically disables explosive dye packs which are hidden in Marked Bills, which is why learning how to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6 is essential if you want to rob a bank or payday loans store.

#3760. Guarding Stars Made A Major Change To The Book's Ending I Don't Understand

Spoilers for the movie Guarding Stars and the book The Bodyguard are ahead! You can stream the film with a Netflix subscription.

I try really hard not to judge a movie or TV show based on its source material and the changes made to it. In fact, I usually love it when a book-to-screen adaptation makes bold updates and takes creative liberties. However, when I watched Netflix’s Guarding Stars, which is based on Katherine Center’s novel, The Bodyguard, I couldn’t help but be baffled by a massive change that was made to the ending.

Alright, let’s get into the endings of these two projects that follow actor Jack Stapleton and his bodyguard, Hannah Brooks – who are played by CW icons Jared Padalecki and Leighton Meester, respectively, in the film – as they go from fake-dating to real love.

In Center’s book, The Bodyguard, after all covers are blown and everyone thinks Jack is safe, he's taken hostage. When Hannah shows up for a date with him, Jack tells her to go away in an effort to keep her safe. Ultimately, she realizes Jack didn’t mean what he said, and that he was in danger. So, she ran back into his home to save him, and to make a long story short, after a fight and a gunshot wound for Hannah, they survived and lived happily ever after.

In the movie on the 2026 Christmas schedule, nearly the same thing happens, except one vital change is made: Jack goes to Hannah’s apartment in New York to confess his love. When he gets there, she tells him she has company and does not share his feelings. Once he leaves, he realizes she was lying and goes back to save her. Ultimately, a similar kind of struggle plays out, and Hannah and Jack make it through safe and only slightly scathed, with Jack taking the gunshot wound instead of Hannah.

On the whole, this movie is very different from its source material. While it keeps the essence intact, a lot of the key elements of the novel are totally changed. However, this final sequence where Jack/Hannah gets taken hostage stays fairly similar; the film just switches who shows up and decides to save whom and who gets shot. So, why change it in the first place?

In the book, I loved that Hannah showed up to Jack’s house and saved him. It really showed off both how good she is at her job and how much she genuinely cares for the actor she was protecting. I also appreciated how that scene addressed her doubt about their relationship and made her realize that Jack really does love her.

In the movie, because Jack is the one who shows up for Hannah, we don’t fully get all of that. However, we do get to see him be a more active participant in this whole fiasco. While she still ultimately saves him in this big mess, it starts with him trying to protect her. To an extent, I get it, because Jack is more involved in the fight. However, what I loved about the book was that Hannah used this situation as the moment where she finally realized their shared feelings and got to kick butt in the process. I wish that's what had happened in the movie.

So, ultimately, while most of the changes in Guarding Stars didn’t bother me at all, this one did a bit. I just can’t understand why they’d swap the genders and have Jack go to save Hannah and keep the rest of the squirmish pretty much the same. However, it’s still a project on the 2026 movie schedule that’s worth a watch, and maybe a debate if you’ve also read the book.

#3759. Walmart’s 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales Are Now Live

If you're thinking of picking up any big-ticket items—whether for yourself or as a gift for someone on your list— I would advise you not to sleep on Walmart's sale. Walmart is the first major retailer to announce and kick off its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale for 2026, and they're actually holding three major shopping events between now and the December holidays.

Walmart will hold three sales between Nov. 12 and Dec. 2, as outlined in a recent press release. The sales will be both online and in-store, and will target a mix of Walmart+ members and general shoppers.

The events will take place on three different dates:

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 1: Nov. 12–15

Available online and in stores starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access beginning online at 12:01 a.m. ET on Nov. 12

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 2: Nov. 23–29

Online only: Nov. 23 starting at 12:01 a.m. ET

Online and in stores: Nov. 27 starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access online beginning Nov. 23 at 12:01 a.m. ET

Walmart's Cyber Monday Deals Event: Nov. 30-Dec. 2

Walmart's physical stores will open at 6:00 a.m. local time on Nov. 27 for their Black Friday events. Of course, they will start online earlier, so make sure to check their website as well.

Walmart says that they will have discounts on electronics, toys, fashion, beauty, home goods, gifts, and everyday essentials. Although the company doesn't provide much in the way of specifics in its press release, last year's sales included discounts on TCL TVs, Dyson vacuums, Dreo appliances, and toys from LEGO.

Walmart's first sale already features plenty of good deals; you don't need to wait for Nov. 27 to start to find some products going for their lowest prices ever. Here are some of the best ones I've found so far:

No. But if you are a Walmart+ member, you'll get early access to the sale. You can sign up for a free 30-day Walmart+ subscription and cancel it afterwards or get the annual plan for $98 ($8.17/month).

Deals will be both online and in the physical stores. There might be deals online that you won't see in-store and vice versa.

The holiday season will see major sales from the same list of retailers that compete for your dollars throughout the year—namely, Best Buy, Target, and Amazon. Each will have its own version of Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales. So far, only Walmart has revealed its plans.

In short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

Black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Now, however, the distinction is almost meaningless: Every major retailer offers sales on both days, which means the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers to monitor the deals, and refer to our Black Friday coverage, where we do all the searching, curating, and price tracking for you.

Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look.

The Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio, which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name.

The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.

Look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.

You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.

The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

Head upstairs to the second floor and enter the Jack of Hearts recording studio. Pass through the lobby and into the control room, then you'll see the Sniper of Perle poster lying on the table beside a fan.

Once you arrive at the nightclub, head through the entrance corridor and look at the back wall. The poster is right there, and one quick scan is all it takes to unlock The Vault's playlist.

#3757. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more."

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

From Ezio Auditore to 17th century witch hunts, Patrice Désilets talks 1666 Amsterdam's devilish origins, everchanging mechanics, and the process of making a game with a community

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Patrice Désilets is known as the father of Assassin's Creed, but his newest baby is his entire world. Panache Digital Games' 1666 Amsterdam finally launched into Early Access in August 2026, the spoils of a hard-won IP battle between Désilets and former employer Ubisoft after he left the studio for the last time in 2013. The timing of its launch seems eerily prescient now that Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe – rumored to be Ubisoft's own witch trials-themed action-adventure – has been reportedly delayed by a year. Having launched into Early Access before Hexe was given a proper reveal, 1666 Amsterdam feels like a bold statement, a flag on the moon of this particular space race: We were here first.

Speaking to me at Gamescom, Xbox controller in-hand to show off the Early Access build that had launched that same week, Désilets reflected on the long road to getting Noa's story into players' hands – even if he still expects it to undergo many more changes on the journey to v1.0.

We're sharing this full interview transcript exclusively with our members, offering an extra peek into Patrice's approach to development. If you'd like to read the whole thing, you can do so simply by signing in, or by registering for free - just enter your email address below.

GamesRadar+: Why don't we first talk about how it feels now to have the game in Early Access after so many years of being in your brain? It must be quite mind-boggling.

Patrice Désilets: It's a mixed thing because it's like, "Oh! It's up there!" [gesturing to the game displayed on the TV]. But on Monday we have to continue working on it. But it's great. At the end there's always some doubts – am I crazy for wanting to do this for 15 years? Should I just move on? But it's like no, no, no! Because it's a good thing that I stuck with it even though it changed so much somehow in those 16 years.

If you think about it, it was my first game right after Assassin's Creed, right? So I was really tainted by Ezio and Altair and the ruleset that we'd built over the years. So at first, [1666 Amsterdam] was all about the devil. Like, you played the devil. And I went back to it in 2020, and was like, "I don't want to talk about that anymore. Back to square one again." [I asked myself] What would be the character that represented that devilish side of the world? Like, oh, witches! And I'm not 'the witch guy' at first, right? But I was like, oh, it's perfect. Let's do with witches what I did with Assassins, and let's create an open world and a badass witch using the broom and not the old lady inside a little hut in the woods. So that's how it all started, and now it's out there and people are giving us feedback. The great part is that our goal now is actually to listen and make it better with them.

With magical combat, city sleuthing, and physical roguelike charms, I can't wait for 1666 Amsterdam

GR+: You mentioned at the hands-on preview that your whole dream behind making Panache was to eventually make a game with the community. So how has the feedback been so far? Like, has it made you think, "okay, now I know what I want to do," even while you're here at Gamescom?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

PD: Just like you didn't have a chance to play it yet, I didn't have a chance to actually look at the feedback yet because I'm here talking with people. What I just learned is that my team is excited in Montreal. They're really already in the [mindset of] "okay, yes, there's this and that we can change." They have ideas. And that's kind of how we work – we work in an iterative process, so we listen to the game, listen to ourselves. So it's not about me and my design, saying, "This is what I want, let's do this!"

There's a lot of things that we tried and ultimately went like, "Ah, you know what, guys, it doesn't work." Like for a while, you didn't play as a cat. Could you imagine? You could possess cats, for a long period of time [in development]. But I was afraid to have a witch and a cat. I was afraid of people going "oh, he's doing cliché stuff there." But like, man, it's a witch! And then what if the cat is the guy from 1999? Because he [the character of Aaron] was just a spectral [humanoid] figure for a long period of time, there to possess people. But what if he's possessing a cat in 1666? And then you'll have the two worlds of 1999 and 1666, two halves woven together all the time, and the relationship between the two characters will make it a whole? And but that's not me being so fucking genius with that, ordering people about. That's not at all how I work. So that's why now [in Early Access], it's just more people telling us, "This is good, this is not that good." We're used to it.

GR+: Talking of changes, I remember last time you mentioned that you lose all Noa's abilities when you die, and that you need to go back and find them all over again in the open world. But it's different now in Early Access?

PD: Yes, because we are listening! We did some playtests and people were like, "Are you fucking crazy? I spent two hours finding all of this, and you removed them all." So what we do now is that for every coffer and curiosity cabinet you find, you get a new type of ability. Once you find them, you're fine. But when you fail, you just redo a big lottery, so you'll have new abilities and some of them will be the same. But you don't have to find them all over again. So you may approach the mission differently this time because you don't have some of the abilities you had. It messes a bit with your brain, like, "Okay, I had the Warp mechanic. I was good in fights and now I'm less physically powerful, but I'm stronger in Compulsion." So you have to approach the mission differently. And when you finish an Esbat – when you finish like a full moon cycle – then you can lock one or two abilities forever.

GR+: So it really does sound like everything is open to – well, not suggestion, but would you say everything is open to discussion when it comes to the making of the game and how you take on community feedback?

PD: [laughs] Well, eventually there's a limit to the listening! If you don't want a cat but a different animal instead, like, no. You're having a cat. The narrative is our thing. The story – we're writing it, and it'll be a surprise for players. But there's always going to be something cool mechanics-wise that we were never aware of, that the community will come up with.

It's the beauty of making games now. We're in Early Access. Okay, it's not finished, we know. So it's part of the process. But real data comes back, not wishful thinking, and we can actually adjust for real, a little ease of play. Our goal is that we have our backlog of ideas and things we want to do. If the community has the same idea and it aligns, this is priority number one [to implement]. Other than that: we have a plan.

#3755. The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the big deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

This is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

For years, Leroy Jethro Gibbs was the face of NCIS. His litany of rules and quirks was the heart and soul of the series, with his trademark head slap being one of them. As he's back in primetime on the Origins spinoff, I'm learning the slap all started with his former co-star, Michael Weatherly.

Mark Harmon spoke on its origins in an interview with Cheat Sheet, and how a bit of improvisation became an iconic recurring bit. Harmon set the scene far back before the 2026 TV schedule, all the way back to the first year of the series:

Michael is a hugely talented actor, as is every member of this cast. My memory of when that happened, we were doing a scene. And he was on a Navy ship and he was talking to a female petty officer. I think this was in year one, early. And he was doing what he does, which is sometimes stay on script and sometimes not. I just reached over and smacked him. I tried to put him back on line. It was an instinct. It wasn’t thought, I didn’t think about it, I just did it.

Funny to think this all started partly because Mark Harmon was frustrated with Michael Weatherly going off script. I could imagine filming days were long enough without improvisation that it could sabotage a scene that was perfectly written as-is. I can empathize with Harmon just wanting to move on, and giving Weatherly a smack on the head to remind him that other people would like to move on as well.

In fairness to Weatherly, Harmon's head slap could've caused a much bigger distraction had he completely broken character and gotten into a fight with his co-star. Fortunately, Harmon confirmed the Tony DiNozzo actor didn't miss a beat, and it became a part of the show's history:

To his credit, he stayed in the scene; he didn’t break. And I didn’t break. And the girl in the scene playing the petty officer, she was shocked, she was surprised. And she stayed there, and we just kept going. And people liked it. And every episode I was smacking him–maybe too much. We still do that occasionally, but sparingly. That’s where it came from.

It may not be the sole reason that NCIS is now a franchise generating billions of dollars across its lifetime, but it certainly contributed. Tony and Gibbs' relationship was one of the show's best parts in its early years, and many still remember it fondly.

What's funny about this story is that Michael Weatherly largely remembers it the same way, but added on detail that Harmon left out. In the moment, no one knew that the head smack was going to be something iconic in NCIS. It was only Season 1, and they were just a few episodes in.

Instead, Weatherly only remembers that he was goofing off, and everyone on set was mad at him afterward for potentially ruining a shot. It wasn't until they saw the head smack in the editing room that producers liked it and decided to make it a part of the episode and the show.

These days, Weatherly's Tony doesn't get a ton of head smacks. He's currently the acting director of the NCIS team, and also occasionally jumping in to lend a hand in investigations. I don't imagine anyone wants to slap the boss man on the back of the head, but I'd be up for seeing someone try.

NCIS continues on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. The entire evening is silly with spinoffs for the crime procedural, so anyone who isn't currently already aware of that should check it out!

#3753. GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

"The decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers."

Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop."

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition."

Though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history". But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off."

It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July, claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.

"99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team."

Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction."

Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.

"I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created."

The games industry has seen a huge number of layoffs in the last few years. A recent report by GDC found that 34% of developers it surveyed had been laid off since 2024. Xbox alone has cut thousands of jobs, with more planned going into January 2027. Most recently, Firaxis, owned by GTA 6 publisher Take Two Interactive, reportedly laid off a third of its staff earlier this week as it works on a new XCOM.

Where where to find and start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6 and earn a stamina upgrade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Big Flush in GTA 6 is an optional mission, but it's well worth your time for a permanent stamina upgrade. You can start this GTA 6 mission from Chapter 1 onwards, and once it's done it's incredibly useful reward will allow you to do energy-draining activities, like running and swimming, for longer. It's also just a fun side mission to do. After finding an odd poster in a men's bathroom stall, you are enlisted to help oddball Dr. Merle to prove his bizarre conspiracy theory that the government is stealing DNA from poop (which is seemingly based on a real report about Putin) and things only get stranger from there.

To start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6, go to the bathroom block toward the north tip of Corsair Key in Mariana County (just north-east of Key Lento). It should be easy to find as it's the only building in Corsair Key. Enter the men's toilet and you'll see a handmade poster on the wall that says "Stop! Don't Flush.

Scan to learn the truth #NOFLUSHERS" with a QR code attached. Use your WaiNK IT app to scan the code and you'll receive a message from an Automated Machine that tells you to reply "TRUTH" to join the No Flushers movement. Select the "Truth" reply and you'll receive another message telling you that whoever is messaging will be at Frank's Waffles in Vice City. If asked, you need to repeat the code: 00-00-02.

You need to meet the mystery No Flusher at Frank's Waffles in the Tequesta neighborhood of Vice City, in Vice-Dale County. When you enter the waffle house, you'll find a man muttering to himself in one of the booths nearest the toilets. However, he seemingly won't appear if it's not night time, as, when I went during the day, the mission icon had a padlock on it and the man wasn't there.

When you get near the man, he covers up whatever he's working on and tells you that he's holding a royal flush. When he asks do you have a "coda for that?," hold LT/LR while looking at the man to bring up the dialogue menu and select the code option with X/A.

The oddball man is Dr. Merle, who quickly ingests a tracking device and begins waffling (no pun intended) about his conspiracy theory that the poop of Leonida citizens isn't actually going to the sewers but is instead going to a secret government DNA siphoning center. He then goes to the corporate-controlled bathroom to deposit the tracking device into the federally-controlled sewers, so you can track where Leonida's bowel movements go to the source of the whole operation.

Once Dr Merle is done in the bathroom, follow him to his van outside. Follow his verbal directions to follow the tracker and it'll take you to the sewage treatment plant in Hamlet in Vice-Dale County. Follow the waypoint to park the van on the coast then follow Dr Merle on foot to the plant.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

When you reach the plant's fence, Dr. Merle begins unlocking a metal gate so that you can get inside and asks you to keep an eye out. Keep an eye on the road on the other side of the gate as a van will soon approach. If the driver stops and asks what you're doing, the best approach is to use the "Defuse" dialogue option to tell the worker you're simply fixing the gate.

Once you're inside the sewage treatment plant ground, you're tasked with finding the tracker. The best approach is to head toward the area highlighted pink on your GTA 6 map until you see the two works chatting. Approach them and, when asked if you are electricians, use the "Lie" dialogue option to go along with their theory. Go through the open metal gate to the left of the works, then slightly right and you'll see a set of double doors. Enter these doors to enter the facility.

Once you get inside Dr. Merle starts to freak out because the tracking device is apparently below your feet, but there's no obvious way to reach it, so he asks you to find a way down. Go up the metal stairs in this room and you'll find a control panel on the platform above. Select Triangle/Y to interact with the panel.

To open the stairs that lead downstairs, all three lights on the left of the control panel need to be turned to green. So, push the buttons next to the two red lights (the middle and bottom ones), to turn them green, then tilt the main lever on the panel. A secret staircase leading downstairs will then open up where Dr.Merle is sitting.

Go down the stairs and you'll enter a room with a large, mysterious-looking chamber. Determined to prove his DNS-siphoning theory is correct, Dr. Merle gets into the chamber– which soon begins to fill with liquid – and asks you to flush him. Press the red button on the control panel in front of the chamber to do so.

Unfortunately, this puts the water authority on your case. They warn over a loudspeaker that the authorities are on their way and that the chamber is highly toxic, so you absolutely should not step inside it. Step inside the chamber and you'll automatically be flushed. You wake up (somehow) outside Jason's House with a notification telling you your max stamina has increased.

Spoilers ahead for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

The Hunger Games movies have entertained audiences for decades now, and we're getting yet another book to screen adaptation with Francis Lawrence's Sunrise on the Reaping. The latest prequel tells the story of Haymitch's games, with actor Joseph Zada perfectly emulating Woody Harrelson. There are still some surprises for those who read the book, including a few references to Lucy Gray from Songbirds and Snakes (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) that weren't in the source material. CinemaBlend spoke to the movie's director about why those changes were made for the latest installment in the franchise.

Years after the original Hunger Games movies, we've returned to Panem thanks to author Suzanne Collins' pair of prequels. First was Songbirds and Snakes, which followed a young President Snow who fell in love with and then lost Rachel Zegler's Lucy Gray Baird. Lucy Gray's fate is left ambiguous in both the film and book, as she disappeared and fled from Snow after winning the 10th Hunger Games.

Sunrise on the Reaping's movie deviates from the book by having Snow mention Lucy Gray by name when talking to Haymitch at Plutarch's home. As you can see in the video above, I had to ask Francis Lawrence about this change, and he told me:

That's not in the book. And that came out of conversations that we had with Suzanne and our screenwriter when we're going through and just talking about, you know, you have to go into every scene and go 'How? Why?' all of that. And we started to question about Snow making this appearance and why him coming in person is so important, especially when he's, you know, not feeling so well. Not to spoil anything. And that's what we came up with, which I was really happy about is this idea of this kind of personal quest that for 40 years he's still been obsessed with what happened to Lucy Gray.

Honestly, this makes a great deal of sense. While Haymitch makes a quick enemy out of Snow during the Chariot sequence that killed Louella, why would the President of Panem (played in this film by Ralph Fiennes) show up in person to intimidate him? This scene was expanded in the film by having Snow specifically talk about Lucy Gray, the District 12 victor and his love interest that he's still seemingly searching for. Whether or not we ever get confirmation about her ultimate fate remains to be seen.

In addition to Snow name-dropping Lucy Gray, we also get another reference to Zegler's character during the funeral scene towards the end of the movie. At the services for the District 12 tributes like Maysilee, the Covey sing "The Old Therebefore," the song Lucy Gray belts out as snakes cover her body at the end of her Games. In our same conversation Lawrence explained how this came about, telling me:

Suzanne is a real music aficionado. And, you know, she obviously was very involved in writing many lyrics for the previous songs and all of that. And has, you know, sort of her mythology of how these songs have been sung and what songs have been passed along. That was one of the ideas too, is that that's the kind of song that you would sing at a funeral, which is partially why Lucy Gray sings it when she thinks that she's gonna die, so that she's almost singing her own funeral song. So, but it's just nice that you, you feel those kind of connections, and it's the same with The Hanging Tree, you hear Lucy Gray singing that, but you've already heard Katniss singing it.

I honestly love this attention to detail. While these are not huge moments in the Hunger Games movies, the way songs are used throughout the franchise helps to make the cinematic universe feel more interconnected. There's a ton of lore within the story of Panem, and these small changes to Sunrise on the Reaping will no doubt be powerful for longtime fans of the YA franchise.

Francis Lawrence mentioned this being a goal in including "The Old Therebefore" in the newest Hunger Games movie, saying:

But that's just a song that she's heard and has been passed down for years, you know, in District 12. So it's just, it's nice how everything interconnects.

Sunrise on the Reaping's reviews have been mixed, but now moviegoing audiences will get to judge the latest Hunger Games flick for themselves. Fans are hoping to see more prequels in the future, but that'll presumably only happen once Suzanne Collins release another novel. Fingers crossed that happens sooner rather than later.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. Fingers crossed that the franchise keeps expanding with more prequels.
